questions.title: Which driver will take pole position for the inaugural Freedom 250 Grand Prix in Washington, DC?
questions.background: Pole position is the first starting spot on the grid, awarded through qualifying.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Resolve to the driver credited with pole position in IndyCar's official qualifying results for the inaugural Freedom 250 Grand Prix, scheduled for August 23, 2026, in Washington, DC. Resolution Date : 2026-08-22 Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the driver's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Four-time champion Alex Palou is on an astonishing 2026 qualifying tear—6 poles in the first 10 rounds including 5 consecutive poles (most recently Road America on June 20) and 3 of 4 street-course wins (St. Pete, Long Beach, Detroit). However, IndyCar's inaugural 1.66-mile, 7-turn National Mall street circuit uses the high-variance 2026 single-lap Fast 6 shootout format across a deep 25+ car field, keeping Palou calibrated at 28% and top-5 total at 62%. Andretti street ace Kyle Kirkwood (2nd in points), breakout Penske qualifier David Malukas (3rd in points, P2 Road America, Fast 12 leader Long Beach), Pato O'Ward (P2 Long Beach), and Long Beach single-lap pole winner Felix Rosenqvist (CGR-allied Honda) complete the top 5, leaving 38% for McLaughlin, Power, Lundgaard, Ericsson, Newgarden, and field.

questions.title: Which Republican U.S. Senate candidate will be reported by August 25, 2026, to have asked AIPAC not to campaign on their behalf?
questions.background: The American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC) is a pro-Israel lobbying organization active in congressional elections. Its political support has historically extended to candidates from both major U.S. parties. The next midterm elections are scheduled for November 2026.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Reporting by established news organizations published by August 25, 2026. Resolution Conditions : Identify the Republican candidate for U.S. Senate in the November 2026 election reported to have requested that AIPAC not run a campaign on their behalf. A request conveyed through the candidate's campaign allies qualifies; merely criticizing AIPAC does not. Accepted Answer Format : The candidate's first and last name.
questions.current_reasoning: Massive 52-day refresh on 2026-08-15 (stale since June 24; resolves Aug 22 / deadline Aug 25) reversing the #1/#2 order completely: (1) Michigan GOP nominee Mike Rogers surges 0.18 -> 0.54 (+0.36, disciplined <=0.55 unconfirmed-report cap) into the overwhelming favorite. On Aug 4, anti-AIPAC progressive Abdul El-Sayed defeated Haley Stevens in Michigan's Democratic Senate primary despite AIPAC spending a record $32M against him; the very next day (Aug 5), the New York Times reported (Political Wire Aug 5; highlighted by Bernie Sanders on CBS Face the Nation Aug 9-10 and Al Jazeera Aug 7) that AIPAC told allies it is weighing 'tens of millions of dollars' to campaign for Mike Rogers in the general election. Rogers is now the ONLY Republican Senate nominee actively facing an imminent, publicized multi-million-dollar AIPAC general-election campaign — in the exact state where AIPAC spending just demonstrably backfired and alienates key Arab-American and America First swing voters, giving Rogers or his campaign allies urgent incentive to quietly ask AIPAC to stay out. (2) Maine Sen. Susan Collins drops sharply 0.42 -> 0.16 (-0.26) because the premise of her June lead collapsed: anti-AIPAC Democratic opponent Graham Platner dropped out in July over a sexual assault allegation and was replaced by populist former state Senate president Troy Jackson (CBS News Jul 25-27), though Collins remains a credible #2 in blue-leaning Maine. (3) Texas GOP nominee Ken Paxton enters at #3 (0.09): San Antonio Express-News (Jul 22) highlights Paxton questioning U.S. funding for Israel and campaigning with anti-AIPAC/Tucker Carlson allies while trailing James Talarico slightly in polls as AIPAC weighs whether to back him after Cornyn's loss. (4) Michael Whatley (NC, 0.03) and MAGA/America First Rep. Mike Collins (GA vs Jon Ossoff, 0.03) round out the Top 5 (sum = 0.85, leaving 0.15 across Jon Husted, Dan Sullivan, and other 2026 GOP Senate nominees).

questions.title: Which humanoid robot will win the opening-day 100-metre race at the 2026 World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing?
questions.background: The World Humanoid Robot Games includes sporting competitions for humanoid robots.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official results or contemporaneous reporting of the opening-day 100-metre race at the 2026 World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing. Resolution Date : 2026-08-22 Accepted Answer Format : String (robot name). Resolve to the humanoid robot reported as the winner of the opening-day 100-metre race.
questions.current_reasoning: Aug 14 Beijing organizing committee press conference (China Daily) confirms the 2026 World Humanoid Robot Games run Aug 22-26 with a massively expanded field of 2,056 robots from 666 teams across 16 countries—teams up 138% YoY and participating robots doubled, including 157 Chinese companies and 200 universities/research institutes—with officials anticipating faster records after humanoids outperformed humans at April's Beijing E-Town Half Marathon. Separately, Reuters/Straits Times (Aug 10) covering Unitree's 6.1B yuan Shanghai IPO still highlights G1, H1, and R1 as Unitree's flagship humanoid models (giving Unitree high IPO visibility incentive, with H1 having demonstrated 10.1 m/s track speed in April). Because the field has doubled to 157 companies and 2,056 robots—magnifying single-race fall, autonomy-multiplier, and newly unveiled 2026 sprinter risks—we trim top-5 concentration from 0.61 to 0.53: Unitree H1 0.26 -> 0.22, Tiangong Ultra 0.20 -> 0.17, Tiangong 2.0 0.05 -> 0.06, Unitree H2 0.06 -> 0.04, Star1 steady at 0.04 (leaving 47% for the expanded field).

questions.title: If Fabinho moves to a new club during the 2026 summer transfer window, which club will he join?
questions.background: Brazilian midfielder Fabinho joined Al-Ittihad in 2023 after spending five years at Liverpool. This question is conditional on him making a permanent move to another club.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official club announcements or regulatory filings confirming Fabinho’s signing. Resolution Rule : Resolve to the first new club officially confirmed as signing Fabinho on a permanent contract between June 1 and September 30, 2026, regardless of his previous contractual status. Loans do not qualify. If no qualifying signing is announced during this period, the question is void. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the destination club.
questions.current_reasoning: Major Aug 6-8 transfer update (Arab News, Globo Esporte, ESPN Brazil, Liverpool.com, Okaz): Al-Ittihad officially announced Fabinho's departure on Aug 6 after he declined reduced-wage renewal terms, making the 32-year-old Brazil World Cup midfielder a free agent expected to choose his next club 'in the coming days.' Crucially, ESPN Brazil (Bruno Andrade, Aug 7) reports a return to Brazil is 'practically impossible' right now—Fabinho has refused to open negotiations with Brazilian clubs, and Palmeiras explicitly ended their interest after targeting Botafogo's Danilo—while confirming his #1 priority is returning to Europe, with MLS and Asia as secondary options for attractive projects. Removing Palmeiras and Fluminense and slashing Flamengo (0.08 -> 0.03) cuts Brazilian clubs from 19% to 3%, shifting our calibrated top-5 toward natural European and MLS free-agent fits: former club Monaco (0.05 -> 0.06), wage-capable Turkish Super Lig contenders Galatasaray (0.05) and Fenerbahce (0.04), residual Flamengo (0.03), and MLS marquee destination Inter Miami (0.03). Because no specific European or MLS club has confirmed active talks yet, total top-5 mass stays low at 0.21 (79% field).

questions.title: Who will win the 2026 Formula One Dutch Grand Prix?
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : The FIA's official race classification or Formula One's official race results for the 2026 Dutch Grand Prix. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the driver officially classified as the winner of the Grand Prix's main race, rather than a qualifying session or sprint race. Accepted Answer Format : The winning driver's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-07-26 Hungarian GP race update (Reuters/Straits Times, Irish Times, Al Jazeera, Khaleej Times, NDTV) provides the decisive technical read heading into the 4-week summer break before Zandvoort (Aug 23, the calendar's closest high-downforce analog to the Hungaroring): McLaren's upgraded package completely dominated race pace, with defending champion Lando Norris winning by 15 seconds over Max Verstappen after overcutting teammate Oscar Piastri, who led early and was cruising in a McLaren 1-2 before a collision with backmarker Carlos Sainz and a lap-56 gearbox failure forced his retirement. Norris jumps from 0.13 to 0.22 (co-favorite) and Piastri enters the top 5 at 0.12 (total McLaren win equity ~34%, tempered by gearbox reliability and Hungary being McLaren's 3-year bogey track). Championship leader Kimi Antonelli remains co-favorite at 0.22 (down slightly from 0.24) after a strong comeback drive to P3 extending his WDC lead to 50 points over Lewis Hamilton and 59 over George Russell. Max Verstappen enters at 0.12 after taking P2 in Hungary ahead of both Mercedes and both Ferraris, with strong home-circuit upside at Zandvoort. Ferrari's race pace trailed McLaren and Red Bull (Charles Leclerc dropped from P2 grid to P4 -> 0.11; Lewis Hamilton finished P4 on track / P5 after a 5s pitlane speeding penalty and VSC strategy error -> ~0.10 just outside top 5). George Russell drops outside the top 5 (~0.08) after stalling at the start and recovering only to P7 behind Isack Hadjar. Top-5 sum = 0.79 (0.21 outside: Hamilton ~0.10, Russell ~0.08, rest of field ~0.03).

questions.title: Which club will sign Ayyoub Bouaddi from Lille during the 2026 summer transfer window?
questions.background: Ayyoub Bouaddi is a midfielder at Lille.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official announcements from the clubs involved or confirmed transfer reporting from a major sports news organization. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the club that completes Bouaddi's permanent transfer from Lille during the 2026 summer transfer window. Transfer negotiations and agreements that remain conditional do not count as completed signings. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the signing club.
questions.current_reasoning: Strong multi-source convergence toward Manchester City from Aug 3-15, tempered just below 0.65 because the deal is not yet officially completed: (1) Florian Plettenberg / Sky Sports Germany (Aug 3) reported Bouaddi reached a full verbal agreement on personal terms with City until 2031; Fabrizio Romano (Aug 7) reported City and Lille are 'very close' to agreement; The Guardian / BBC Sport (Aug 11) reported City are closing in on a ~EUR 100m (GBP 85m) move, while AS/FootballTransfers (Aug 10) cited up to EUR 130m. (2) Two decisive structural catalysts landed: Rodri completed his move from Man City to Barcelona (resolved market #243962), Chelsea's deadline for Enzo Fernandez—Maresca's main alternative target—passed on Aug 15 (Manchester Evening News Aug 15), and Arsenal shifted focus away from Bouaddi (Sky Sport Aug 3) after completing Bruno Guimaraes (resolved market #108618). (3) Still, Lille manager Davide Ancelotti played Bouaddi 45 minutes in a friendly vs. Everton on Aug 15 and confirmed 'there are negotiations' and 'interest from so many clubs' while hoping he stays, so keeping Manchester City capped at 0.64 (up from 0.52) with hijack mass across Arsenal (0.11, down from 0.18), Liverpool (0.07), Manchester United (0.06), Chelsea (0.05), and 0.07 residual (Real Madrid/PSG/other).
